title: SH0ES 2022: Cepheid-supernova H0 is 73.04 ± 1.04 km/s/Mpc
summary: Riess and colleagues report a baseline H0 of 73.04 ± 1.04 km/s/Mpc from HST Cepheids and 42 nearby supernovae, and a 5-sigma difference from the Planck plus Lambda-CDM prediction.
body: The abstract of Riess and colleagues (SH0ES) reports HST Cepheids in the hosts of 42 Type Ia supernovae at z < 0.01, calibrated with Gaia EDR3 parallaxes, masers in NGC 4258, and detached eclipsing binaries in the Large Magellanic Cloud. The baseline result from the Cepheid-supernova sample is H0 = 73.04 ± 1.04 km/s/Mpc, including systematics. With the tip of the red-giant branch the abstract also gives 72.53 ± 0.99. Including high-redshift supernovae it gives H0 = 73.30 ± 1.04 and q0 = −0.51 ± 0.024. It says there is a 5-sigma difference with the H0 predicted by Planck plus Lambda-CDM, and that the source of the discrepancy between the direct and the cosmological routes remains unknown. The 73.04 figure is the team's distance-ladder measurement. The Planck prediction is the other route named in the abstract. This card does not copy a Planck H0 numeral from a different paper.
